claims.text: An ordered intermetallic Pt–Ni catalyst with a Pt-rich surface will have greater HER and HOR catalytic activity than pure Pt.
An ordered intermetallic Pt–Ni catalyst with a Pt-rich surface will be more durable during HER and HOR than pure Pt.
Thermal annealing of disordered Pt–Ni nanoparticles can induce intermetallic ordering.
Thermal annealing, potentially combined with selective acid leaching, can produce a Pt-rich skin on Pt–Ni nanoparticles.
The proposed treatment produces an ordered intermetallic core with a Pt-rich surface.
An ordered Pt–Ni core with a Pt-rich surface alters the local electronic structure of surface Pt atoms.
The restructured Pt-rich skin modulates the d-band center of surface Pt atoms.
Modulation of the surface-Pt d-band center moves hydrogen adsorption energies closer to the optimum for HER and HOR.
More nearly optimal hydrogen adsorption energies reduce HER and HOR overpotentials.
The Pt-rich ordered structure improves resistance to dissolution or structural degradation.
The treated Pt–Ni catalyst will exhibit lower onset overpotentials than pure Pt.
The treated Pt–Ni catalyst will exhibit higher HER and HOR exchange current densities than pure Pt.
The treated Pt–Ni catalyst will degrade more slowly during extended operation than pure Pt.
The predicted benefits apply in acidic environments.
The catalytic benefits may depend on alloy composition, annealing conditions, and nanoparticle morphology.
Performance in alkaline conditions or with other catalyst supports is undetermined.
